title: 25-year Amazon drought experiment reveals rainforest's vulnerability to extreme conditions
summary: The 25-year Esecaflor Project in Brazil's Amazon, which diverted 50% of rainwater from a one-hectare study area since 2001, shows significant die-off of large trees and potential transformation into a degraded forest ecosystem rather than savanna. The experimental structure was removed two years ago
takeaways: Duration: 25 years (started 2001); structure removed ~2 years ago (2024)
Method: 6,000 transparent plastic panels diverting ~50% rainfall for 2 decades
Outcome: significant large-tree die-off; forest shifted to new equilibrium (degraded forest, not savanna)
Longest-running, most extensive tropical forest drought study conducted
Monitoring: soil, air, tree growth, sap flow, roots; two 40-meter towers with NASA radar

title: Climate science declares 1.5C warming target unachievable; political consensus lacks acknowledgment
summary: The UN declared the Paris Agreement's 1.5°C warming target is unachievable even with immediate emission cuts; best-case scenarios show 1.8°C warming. Despite this scientific consensus, leaders at COP31 in Turkey maintain political support for the target, invoking slogans like "keep 1.5 alive."
takeaways: Best-case scenario with immediate cuts: 1.8°C warming
Only massive carbon removal could theoretically return warming to 1.5°C

Political reluctance to formally abandon goal guiding climate negotiations over decade

title: Atmospheric oxygen reveals strengthening ocean carbon sink since 1990
summary: Analysis of 30 years of atmospheric oxygen data shows the ocean carbon sink strengthened substantially, while the terrestrial carbon sink stagnated. The ocean absorbed approximately 35% of fossil fuel emissions, with the ocean sink strengthening roughly 0.63 billion tonnes per decade.
takeaways: Ocean absorbed average 2.8 billion tonnes carbon annually
